prize_parts.citation: For discoveries of the physiology of the incretin hormone GLP-1 and its development into therapies for type 2 diabetes and obesity

statement.case_for: All six openings put GLP-1 first, and I agree on the merits rather than because of that unanimity. It is the rare complete arc from hormone physiology (proglucagon processing, glucose-dependent insulin secretion, appetite and gastric effects) to drugs that have changed diabetes and obesity care, with randomized outcome evidence for cardiovascular and renal benefit. The mechanism is stable, replicated, and the timing is not premature. A single-achievement prize that spans physiology and its translation is a coherent reading of the will of the prize, and it keeps the configuration within three names.
statement.case_against: The credit problem is real and I cannot dismiss it. Mojsov's identification of the active GLP-1(7-36) peptide and Habener's group's work on proglucagon and its processing are central, and Habener is absent from the credited names, so any three-person set is open to the charge of unfairness. Including Knudsen also invites the objection that the committee is rewarding industry drug development more than a discovery, and which of the physiology and the medicine the citation should emphasise is a genuine judgment call. If the committee insists on a discovery-only reading, the Mojsov version is more defensible than mine.

responses.point: Drucker, Holst and Mojsov are the most defensible trio, because Knudsen's contribution is drug development rather than discovery and Habener is not credited.
responses.response: I take this seriously and it is the strongest counter to my own opening. Where I differ is that the prize's criterion is a discovery of benefit to humankind, and the conversion of native GLP-1, with a half-life of minutes, into a once-weekly agent was itself an inventive step requiring new insight into albumin binding and DPP-4 resistance. It was not routine engineering. I would still hold Knudsen over Mojsov, but I accept that the physiology-only trio is the main competing configuration and I would not treat the choice as a point of principle.

responses.point: Drucker, Holst and Mojsov form a coherent three-person configuration, with Knudsen a credible alternative, and the history cannot be resolved from the list text alone.
responses.response: I agree that the history cannot be settled from the supplied text, and your candour about relying on recollection is appropriate. My qualification is that Mojsov's priority is itself contested against the Habener group, so including her resolves one attribution dispute by importing another. Your ranking of the unfolded protein response second is a fair alternative view; I place it behind the CAR-T and optogenetics cases because its translational reach is still thinner, though I do not think that is a decisive weakness for a basic-discovery prize.

responses.point: Drucker, Holst and Knudsen are central, with Knudsen the drug-development step, and Mojsov's priority cannot be resolved from the supplied text.
responses.response: We reach the same trio, and I agree the Mojsov question cannot be settled here. Where I would push back is on your CAR-T trio with Rosenberg: his adoptive cell transfer and TIL work is a distinct line from the costimulated chimeric receptor, and adding him to fill the third place weakens the clarity of the citation, while Eshhar remains omitted. If CAR-T is taken up, a June and Sadelain pair is the cleaner attribution.

responses.point: GLP-1 is a complete arc and Drucker, Holst and Mojsov best represent the physiological discovery, with Knudsen possibly a separate prize-worthy component.
responses.response: I agree with the arc and with Knudsen being a distinct component. The difference is whether that component belongs in this prize or is left out, and I would keep it in because the clinical result is the reason the physiology is now prize-relevant. I also note your placement of cGAS-STING fourth; I think its therapeutic translation is too early to compete with the top three, though the basic discovery by Chen is clean.

uncertainties: Fair allocation among Drucker, Holst, Mojsov, Habener and Knudsen, given that Habener is not in the credited names and Mojsov's priority is disputed.
Whether the committee should recognise a discovery-only core or include the drug-development step in the citation.
If GLP-1 is settled, whether optogenetics (six credited people, tool rather than disease discovery) or CAR-T (Eshhar uncredited) is the better second candidate for a later year.
statement.conflict_note: No specific conflict is apparent from the provided profile. My research (single-cell genomics, brain atlases, spatial transcriptomics) does not overlap with the shortlisted GLP-1, CAR-T or optogenetics candidates, and none of the credited names appears among my documented co-authors. Optogenetics is a tool used in neuroscience, a field adjacent to mine, but I have no documented involvement.
